messages:
anya: Heads-up — profiling from the canary last night shows a weird p95 spike when admission fills and KV-prefetch is active. small thread to sync on ideas.

sam: saw that in infra dashboards, p50 mostly fine but p95 jumped from 120ms -> 420ms during a short window. suspect batch formation + token budget interplay.

marta: Log excerpt I pulled: `admit_decision=soft_reject` then a flurry of prefetch requests that hit KV miss rates. snippet: 
```
[2024-11-07T03:12:11Z] request=abc admit=soft_reject reason=token_budget contention=high kv_prefetch=true kv_miss=0.42 batch_size=8
[2024-11-07T03:12:11Z] request=def admit=queue hold=probation_ms=1200
```

kai: interesting — when prefetch miss > 0.3 we see more microbatches forming because the runtime waits for KV resolution, which stretches queues and causes soft 429s to cluster.

anya: proposal: reconcile token budget accounting so prefetched tokens count toward the admission window, but add a short probation window for prefetched requests so they don't immediately consume full lease. config proposal below.

sam: share config plz.

marta: quick draft (for canary):
```
admit:
  token_budget_per_worker: 1500
  kv_prefetch_counted: true
  prefetch_probation_ms: 800
  soft_429_rate_limit: 0.07   # fraction of total admits to return soft 429 per sec
  decay_per_sec: 0.9         # decay factor for soft window
  admit_grace_batching: true
```

kai: I like probation_ms. Also add a heuristic: prefer admitting prefetched requests into the next microbatch even if that delays batch start up to 10ms, to improve batch packing and reduce wasted KV cycles.

anya: right — microbatch delay <= 10ms cap. We'll measure change in tokens/sec and p95. Expected tradeoff: tiny p50 bump, p95 improvement if prefetch hits line up.

sam: can we simulate? I ran a replay with 10k requests and toggled prefetch_counted on/off. Quick numbers:
- baseline (prefetch not counted): p95 420ms, throughput 9.3k tok/s
- prefetch_counted + probation 800ms + microbatch-delay=10ms: p95 210ms, throughput 9.0k tok/s

marta: that's promising — less than 5% throughput drop, big p95 gain. We should still watch for oscillation where soft 429s cluster after probation expires.

kai: agree. Add smoothing for soft_429 decision: make it probabilistic with exponential backoff. Pseudocode: 
```
if token_budget < threshold:
  prob = min(1, base_prob * (1 + recent_missed_prefetches))
  if rand() < prob: return soft_429
```

anya: experiment plan: roll to canary pool A (10% traffic) for 2h with config above + probabilistic soft 429, collect: p50/p95 latency, 429 rate, KV hit/miss, batch size distribution, tokens/sec. Stop if 429 rate > 0.2 or p95 > 1s.

marta: add monitoring queries: 
```
- sum(rate(soft_429_total[1m])) / sum(rate(requests_total[1m]))
- histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(response_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (pool)
- avg(batch_size) by (pool)
- kv_miss_rate = sum(kv_miss) / sum(kv_access)
```

sam: small implementation note: kernel selection hints need to be passed through admit path so that we don't form batches with incompatible kernels (that caused regressions last month). I'll add kernel_hint to the admit record.

kai: thanks — that should avoid the kernel-handoff p95 blip. Also let's log an admit_reason tag: `prefetch_probation`, `soft_429`, or `accepted`. Makes postmortem easier.

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: runtime-canary-v3 -> pool-a at 2024-11-07T09:00:00Z by @anya.

anya: action items: @sam to run canary replay and validate metrics; @marta to add dashboards/alerts for soft_429 ratio and probation expirations; @kai to patch admit record with kernel_hint + admit_reason tags; I'll watch for regressions and roll back if thresholds hit.

sam: starting replay now, will post initial numbers in ~30m. :rocket:

marta: I'll create the dashboard tile and a PagerDuty escalation for soft_429_rate > 0.15.

kai: PR for admit tags incoming.

anya: thanks all — short sync tomorrow if canary looks flaky. :thumbsup:
